claim: Hist2h2be (H2be) is a replication-independent histone variant expressed exclusively by olfactory chemosensory neurons.
source_text: We have identified a replication-independent histone variant, Hist2h2be (referred to herein as H2be ), which is expressed exclusively by olfactory chemosensory neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations including ISH and expression analyses shown in Figures 1 and 2, demonstrating exclusive expression in olfactory neurons.

claim: H2BE levels are heterogeneous among olfactory neurons but stereotyped according to the identity of the co-expressed olfactory receptor (OR).
source_text: Levels of H2BE are heterogeneous among olfactory neurons, but stereotyped according to the identity of the co-expressed olfactory receptor (OR).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by quantitative fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2F,G, demonstrating that each OR is consistently associated with a stereotyped level of H2BE.

claim: Changes in H2be expression affect olfactory function and OR representation in the adult olfactory epithelium.
source_text: Gain- and loss-of-function experiments demonstrate that changes in H2be expression affect olfactory function and OR representation in the adult olfactory epithelium.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through behavioral testing (Figure 3D), gene expression analysis (Figure 4), and OR frequency measurements (Figures 4D,E and 5G,I) in H2be-KO and H2be-GF mice.

claim: H2BE expression is reduced by sensory activity.
source_text: We show that H2BE expression is reduced by sensory activity
evidence_reasoning: Supported by unilateral naris occlusion experiments (Figure 8A,B) and odor exposure experiments (Figure 8D-F) showing reduced H2BE levels in stimulated neurons.

claim: H2BE promotes neuronal cell death such that inactive olfactory neurons display higher levels of the variant and shorter life spans.
source_text: it promotes neuronal cell death, such that inactive olfactory neurons display higher levels of the variant and shorter life spans
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by apoptosis analysis (Figure 7C,E) and BrdU survival studies (Figure 7D,F) showing that H2BE levels correlate with cell death rates and neuronal longevity.

claim: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) of H2BE differ from those of canonical H2B.
source_text: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) of H2BE differ from those of the canonical H2B, consistent with a role for H2BE in altering transcription.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by immunofluorescence and western blot analyses (Figure 14) showing inverse correlation between H2BE and H2B-Lys5-Me levels.

claim: H2be modulates olfactory neuron population dynamics to adapt the OR repertoire to the environment.
source_text: We propose a physiological function for H2be in modulating olfactory neuron population dynamics to adapt the OR repertoire to the environment.
evidence_reasoning: This is a proposed model based on integration of multiple experimental findings including activity-dependent H2BE regulation, effects on neuronal longevity, and changes in OR frequencies.

claim: Patterns of light stimuli reaching each eye are essential for activity-dependent refinement of ocular dominance columns in the visual cortex during perinatal development.
source_text: Pioneering experiments in the visual system showed that patterns of light stimuli reaching each of the two eyes are essential for the activity-dependent refinement of ocular dominance columns in the visual cortex during perinatal development
evidence_reasoning: This claim is attributed to prior work by Hubel and Wiesel, 1977, as indicated by the citation.

claim: Experience-dependent plasticity participates in the functional maturation of auditory, somatosensory, and olfactory systems.
source_text: Similarly, experience-dependent plasticity has been shown to participate in the functional maturation of other sensory systems, including the auditory, somatosensory, and olfactory systems
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by reference to Hensch, 2004, indicating it draws from prior published work.

claim: Environmental stimuli can significantly affect adult brain structures, leading to adaptive and maladaptive changes in sensory responses.
source_text: In addition to their important role in shaping sensory circuits during development, environmental stimuli can also significantly affect adult brain structures, leading to adaptive as well as maladaptive changes in sensory responses
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citations to Buonomano and Merzenich, 1998; Ramachandran and Hirstein, 1998; Moseley and Flor, 2012.

claim: Individual olfactory neurons express a single OR allele chosen through a largely stochastic process.
source_text: Individual olfactory neurons express a single OR allele chosen through a largely stochastic process
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Chess et al., 1994.

claim: The olfactory epithelium of mammals displays continuous neurogenesis throughout adulthood.
source_text: The olfactory epithelium of mammals displays continuous neurogenesis throughout adulthood, such that a slow dividing olfactory neural stem cell population continuously replaces mature olfactory neurons that have variable, though finite, life spans
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to Kondo et al., 2010.

claim: The H2be mRNA possesses a long 3′-untranslated region (UTR) and a poly-A tail.
source_text: The H2be mRNA possesses a long 3′-untranslated region (UTR) and a poly-A tail.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation from molecular characterization of the H2be transcript.

claim: H2BE displays only five amino-acid differences with the canonical mouse H2B protein.
source_text: H2BE displays only five amino-acid differences with the canonical mouse H2B protein
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by sequence alignment shown in Figure 1E.

claim: For 73% of the tested ORs, neurons expressing the same OR display significantly less variation with each other in their H2BE level than is observed within the entire MOE neuronal population.
source_text: Indeed, for 73% of the tested ORs, neurons expressing the same OR display significantly less variation with each other in their H2BE level than is observed within the entire MOE neuronal population (p<0.05 after false-discovery rate [FDR] correction; 1-tailed F-test).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical analysis of quantitative fluorescence microscopy data from 42 specific OR genes.

claim: H2be-KO mice learn odor discrimination tasks more slowly and perform less efficiently than controls.
source_text: Training of H2be-KO mice and littermate controls to discriminate between odors for a water reward revealed that H2be-KO mice learn the task more slowly and perform less efficiently than the controls, suggesting a defect in olfactory function
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by behavioral testing data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Loss of H2be does not cause gross defects in odor-evoked signaling.
source_text: To investigate a potential defect in olfactory signal transduction, we performed electro-olfactograms on MOEs from H2be-KO and heterozygous littermates (Figure 3E) but found no obvious anomalies, indicating that the observed phenotype is not due to gross defects in odor-evoked signaling.
evidence_reasoning: Based on electro-olfactogram measurements shown in Figure 3E.

claim: A large number of ORs are up-regulated in the olfactory epithelia of H2be-KO mice.
source_text: The highly significant enrichment of the 'olfactory detection' gene category (FDR-adjusted p=2 × 10−17) reveals that a large number of ORs may be up-regulated in the olfactory epithelia of H2be-KO mice, which we indeed confirmed by quantitative PCR on a subset of genes
evidence_reasoning: Supported by microarray analysis and confirmed by qPCR (Figure 4B).

claim: OR expression differences between WT and H2be-KO mice increase dramatically with age.
source_text: Interestingly, a comparison of gene expression at 6 months with an earlier age of 5 weeks revealed that OR expression differences between WT and H2be-KO mice increase dramatically with age
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by microarray analysis at two different time points shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Expression differences observed for various ORs in H2be-KO and WT mice correlate with the level of H2BE with which they are normally co-expressed.
source_text: Remarkably, expression differences observed for various ORs in H2be-KO and WT mice were also found to correlate with the level of H2BE with which they are normally co-expressed: ORs with increased expression in H2be-KO mice are associated with high levels of H2BE, while ORs with decreased or unchanged expression appear associated with low H2BE levels
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4F combining microarray and fluorescence microscopy data.

claim: H2BE expression is initiated well after OR expression during neuronal development.
source_text: Analysis of the onset of H2BE relative to ORs normally associated with high levels of H2BE revealed that H2BE expression is initiated well after OR expression
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by developmental expression analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: Loss of H2be increases the life span of mature neurons.
source_text: Analysis of active-CASP3-labeled mature olfactory neurons in H2be-KO and littermate controls revealed a 45% lower frequency of apoptosis in the mutant epithelium... Moreover, analysis of the life span of 5-bromo-2′-deoxyuridine (BrdU)-labeled neurons revealed a significantly higher survival rate in H2be-KO mice compared to controls... These results indicate that the loss of H2be increases the life span of mature neurons.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by apoptosis measurements (Figure 7C) and BrdU survival analysis (Figure 7D).

claim: Ectopic overexpression of H2be results in increased apoptosis and reduced neuronal survival.
source_text: similar analyses in H2be-GF mice revealed a twofold higher rate of apoptosis among mature neurons (Figure 7E) and a significantly reduced survival rate compared to Flag-H2be mice
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by apoptosis and BrdU survival analyses in H2be-GF mice (Figures 7E,F).

claim: Unilateral naris occlusion results in dramatically higher H2BE expression on the closed side of the epithelium relative to the open side.
source_text: Upon analysis of H2BE in the MOE of these mice, we observed dramatically higher H2BE expression on the closed side of the epithelium relative to the open side.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by fluorescence microscopy analysis shown in Figure 8A,B.

claim: Olfactory stimulation of specific neurons results in a relative reduction in their nuclear H2BE levels.
source_text: After 3 weeks of exposure to the odor mixture or mineral oil, the four stimulated neuronal subtypes showed significantly reduced levels of H2BE compared to the same subtypes in control mice... Thus, olfactory stimulation of specific neurons results in a relative reduction in their nuclear H2BE levels.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by odor exposure experiments and fluorescence microscopy (Figures 8D-F).

claim: H2be gene expression is inversely related to neuronal activity.
source_text: These analyses revealed a significant negative correlation between the two markers, further supporting the view that H2be gene expression is inversely related to neuronal activity
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by correlation analysis between GAP43-mCherry and tyrosine hydroxylase in glomeruli (Figure 8G,H).

claim: H2BE levels are cAMP-dependent.
source_text: In Adcy3(+/+) mice, Olfr1508+ neurons contain extremely low H2BE levels (left, arrowheads), while in Adcy3(−/−) mice, Olfr1508+ neurons frequently contain extremely high levels (right, arrowhead), indicating that cAMP participates in the negative regulation of H2BE.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by analysis of H2BE levels in Adcy3-null mice (Figure 9A).

claim: H2BE levels are not Ca2+-dependent.
source_text: Analysis of β-GAL+ (TAU-LACZ) and GAP43-mCherry intensities within glomeruli revealed that Cnga2− neurons (β-GAL+; arrowheads) do not have higher levels of GAP43-mCherry than Cnga2+ neurons (β-GAL−), indicating that H2be expression is not negatively regulated by Ca2+ signaling.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by analysis in Cnga2-null mice (Figure 9B).

claim: ORs that are down-regulated following UNO are normally co-expressed with high levels of H2BE, while up-regulated ORs are normally co-expressed with low H2BE levels.
source_text: Remarkably, this analysis revealed that ORs that are down-regulated following UNO are normally co-expressed with high levels of H2BE, while up-regulated ORs are normally co-expressed with low H2BE levels
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by correlation analysis shown in Figure 10E,F combining UNO microarray data with H2BE level measurements.

claim: FLAG-H2BE is almost entirely chromatin-bound rather than present in soluble nucleoplasm.
source_text: Fractionation of unfixed MOE cell nuclei from Flag-H2be and H2be-GF transgenic mice showed that FLAG-H2BE is present at barely detectable levels in soluble nucleoplasm and is instead almost entirely chromatin-bound
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by nuclear fractionation and western blot analysis (Figure 13A).

claim: H2BE is widely distributed throughout the nucleus and not confined to nuclear puncta.
source_text: High-resolution confocal imaging of neuronal nuclei in the MOE of Flag-H2be mice revealed that H2BE is not confined to nuclear puncta, but rather is widely distributed throughout the nucleus
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by confocal microscopy (Figure 13D).

claim: The protein-coding regions of histone genes are particularly enriched for H2BE, while those of OR and vomeronasal receptor genes are relatively devoid of the variant.
source_text: Interestingly, these analyses and subsequent qPCR experiments revealed that the protein-coding regions of histone genes are particularly enriched for H2BE, while those of OR and vomeronasal receptor (VR) genes are relatively devoid of the variant
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by genome-wide ChIP analysis and qPCR (Figures 13F-H).

claim: Neurons expressing a high level of H2BE display conspicuously low H2B-Lys5-Me immunoreactivity, and vice versa.
source_text: Analysis of H2BE and H2B-Lys5-Me levels in Flag-H2be MOEs revealed a striking inverse correlation between the two staining patterns, such that neurons expressing a high level of H2BE display conspicuously low H2B-Lys5-Me immunoreactivity, and vice versa
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by dual immunofluorescence analysis (Figure 14A,B).

claim: H2BE receives less Lys5 methylation and acetylation compared to canonical H2B.
source_text: Further analyses revealed that the presence of H2BE causes a similar reduction in the level of acetylation at Lys5, indicating that the variant also receives less of this modification compared to canonical H2B
evidence_reasoning: Based on immunofluorescence and western blot analyses showing reduced Lys5-Me and Lys5-Ac in H2BE-expressing neurons.

claim: H2BE appears to undergo higher levels of ubiquitination at Lys120 compared to canonical H2B, though the association is correlative but not causative.
source_text: In contrast, H2BE appears to undergo higher levels of ubiquitination at Lys120, though analyses of the modification in H2be-KO and H2be-GF mice indicate that the association is correlative but not causative
evidence_reasoning: Based on analysis of Lys120 ubiquitination in H2be-KO and H2be-GF mice, indicating correlation without causation.

claim: The absence of odor-evoked activity of specific MOE neuronal populations leads to increased H2BE expression, and in turn changes in transcription and reduced neuronal life span.
source_text: Our data uncover a chromatin-based pathway in which the absence of odor-evoked activity of specific MOE neuronal populations leads to increased H2BE expression, and in turn changes in transcription and reduced neuronal life span.
evidence_reasoning: This is an integrative conclusion based on multiple experimental findings including UNO experiments, activity measurements, gene expression analysis, and longevity studies.

claim: H2BE plays a key role in modulating activity dependent changes, but is likely part of a larger pathway.
source_text: our findings that changes in transcription and OR frequency following unilateral naris occlusion are significantly reduced but not eliminated in H2be-KO mice indicate that H2BE plays a key role in modulating activity dependent changes, but is likely part of a larger pathway.
evidence_reasoning: Based on comparison of UNO effects in WT and H2be-KO mice (Figure 11), showing partial but not complete elimination of activity-dependent changes.

claim: Neurons expressing ORs associated with environmentally salient odors increase in relative abundance over time due to enhanced longevity, while neurons expressing infrequently activated ORs have a shortened life span and become less abundant.
source_text: A scenario thus emerges according to which neurons expressing ORs associated with environmentally salient odors are frequently active and may increase in relative abundance over time due to enhanced longevity, while neurons expressing infrequently activated ORs have a shortened life span, mediated in part by H2BE, and become less abundant
evidence_reasoning: This is a model synthesized from multiple experimental findings including activity-dependent H2BE regulation, effects on longevity, and OR frequency changes.

claim: Differential longevity among olfactory sensory neurons may provide a mechanism by which individuals with similar genomes adapt to diverse olfactory environments.
source_text: Differential longevity among olfactory sensory may provide an effective mechanism by which individuals with similar genomes adapt to diverse olfactory environments, facilitating enhanced sensitivity to odors important for survival.
evidence_reasoning: This is a proposed functional interpretation of the experimental findings, representing a speculative model about the adaptive significance of the observed phenomena.

claim: H2BE replacement of canonical H2B within olfactory chromatin is widespread, but most extensive within transcriptionally active loci.
source_text: Together, our results support a model in which H2BE replacement of canonical H2B within olfactory chromatin is widespread, but most extensive within transcriptionally active loci.
evidence_reasoning: Based on ChIP analysis showing H2BE enrichment near promoters of highly expressed genes and depletion at silent OR/VR loci (Figure 13E-H).

claim: OR-derived basal activity may be a significant contributor to the control of H2BE levels and olfactory neuronal longevity.
source_text: Thus, along with odor-evoked activity, OR-derived basal activity may be a significant contributor to the control of H2BE levels and, in turn, of olfactory neuronal longevity.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation based on comparison of Adcy3-null and UNO effects, suggesting a possible role for basal activity.

claim: H2BE's action in affecting cellular longevity requires an olfactory-specific cellular context.
source_text: Transgene-expressing cells showed no increase in cell death compared to control cells overexpressing the canonical H2b or containing no transgene (not shown), suggesting that H2BE's action in affecting cellular longevity requires an olfactory-specific cellular context.
evidence_reasoning: Based on cell culture experiments showing no toxic effects of H2BE overexpression in non-olfactory cells.

claim: The mouse main olfactory epithelium detects large arrays of chemical cues through the expression of a large family of olfactory receptor genes.
source_text: The MOE detects large arrays of chemical cues through the expression of a large family of olfactory receptor (OR) genes
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation to Buck and Axel, 1991.

claim: H2be is expressed exclusively in the MOE and VNO among 61 mouse tissues examined.
source_text: Profile of H2be mRNA levels in 61 mouse tissues (listed, right), showing exclusive expression in MOE and VNO.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by tissue expression profiling data shown in Figure 1D from GNF/BioGPS database.

claim: The Flag-H2be transgenic allele is expressed at a level similar to the endogenous H2be alleles.
source_text: A primer pair specific for the Flag-tagged transgenic allele produces a normalized signal of approximately 1, indicating similar per-allele expression levels for the transgenic and endogenous H2be alleles.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by qPCR analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Each OR tested is consistently and reproducibly associated with a stereotyped level of H2BE in mature neurons.
source_text: Strikingly, each OR tested appears consistently and reproducibly associated with a stereotyped level of H2BE in mature neurons
evidence_reasoning: Based on quantitative fluorescence microscopy analysis of 42 ORs across multiple animals and tissue sections (Figure 2G).

claim: H2be-KO mice appear healthy and fertile.
source_text: H2be-KO mice appear healthy and fertile.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation from maintaining the H2be-KO mouse line.

claim: Loss of H2be does not cause gross defects in OR gene choice or stabilization of OR gene choice.
source_text: Next, we further analyzed H2be-KO mice for evidence of defects in choice, or in stabilization of OR gene choice. We found no defects in OR co-expression frequencies
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by analysis of OR co-expression frequencies shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The initial BrdU labeling frequency of H2be-GF neurons is approximately 2.9-fold higher than that observed in control neurons, reflecting an elevated rate of neurogenesis.
source_text: Remarkably, the initial BrdU labeling frequency of H2be-GF neurons is approximately 2.9-fold higher than that observed in control neurons, reflecting an elevated rate of neurogenesis, presumably a consequence of the increased rate of apoptosis
evidence_reasoning: Based on BrdU labeling analysis (Figure 7G) with interpretation that increased neurogenesis compensates for increased apoptosis.

claim: Overexpression of H2be or Flag-H2be at high levels in cultured fibroblast or embryonic kidney cells shows no increase in cell death compared to control cells.
source_text: To ensure that the observed increase in apoptosis in transgenic epithelia is not due to a non-specific toxic effect of the overexpressed histone, we expressed H2be or Flag-H2be at high levels in cultured fibroblast (NIH-3T3) or embryonic kidney (HEK-293T) cells. Transgene-expressing cells showed no increase in cell death compared to control cells overexpressing the canonical H2b or containing no transgene
evidence_reasoning: Based on cell viability analysis in cultured cells expressing H2BE transgenes.

claim: FLAG-H2BE protein is normally integrated into chromatin as part of nucleosomes.
source_text: Fractionation of unfixed MOE cell nuclei from Flag-H2be and H2be-GF transgenic mice showed that FLAG-H2BE is present at barely detectable levels in soluble nucleoplasm and is instead almost entirely chromatin-bound
evidence_reasoning: Chromatin-bound localization and co-immunoprecipitation with core histones (Figure 13A,B) indicates normal nucleosome incorporation.
